---
title: Kevin Tsai — 25-Min Prep Sheet
format: pdf
---

**Kevin:** Senior data & AI leader, Genmab (antibody therapeutics). Builds production data platforms + analytics. Wharton EMBA class of 2028. Former BMS supervisor. Warm relationship.

**Your goal:** reconnect → hear his take on the market → make the ask (Genmab opening + forwardable intro).

---

## Time Budget

| Min | What |
|-----|------|
| 0–3 | Warm reconnect — thank him, mention something specific about Genmab or Wharton |
| 3–10 | Let Kevin talk: Genmab move, what he's building, EMBA |
| 10–18 | Your update + his perspective on the 2026 market |
| 18–23 | The ask |
| 23–25 | Next steps — offer to send a one-pager |

---

## Talking Points (yours — ~30s each, pick and choose)

1. **PhD finish line.** Defending August 2026, Epidemiology and Biostatistics. One-sentence version of your most industry-legible thesis result. (Draft: *"My dissertation builds an explainable multimodal AI model for severe TBI outcome prediction — fusing imaging, physiology, and EHR into one framework and making the model's reasoning auditable for clinicians."*)
2. **What's grown since BMS.** Anchor to what Kevin knew you doing, then name what's new: Bayesian UQ at Dow, real-world evidence / multi-site EHR harmonization at UTHealth, DILI prediction at Genentech.
3. **What you're targeting.** Biomedical AI/ML in biopharma or RWE/outcomes. Calibrate to him — both map to Genmab's world.
4. **Why industry, why now.** Short + honest. Something like: *"I've always been pulled toward problems where the model actually ships. The dissertation is that for me in academia; I'm ready to make that the default."*
5. **Aperture.** Location flexibility, open to individual contributor or lead, pharma/biotech/health-tech.

---

## Questions (pick 4–5 — leave room for conversation)

**Open with these:**
- "How's the move to Genmab been? What pulled you there from BMS?"
- "What are you actually building right now — and what does your team look like?"
- "How is Wharton fitting alongside the day job?"

**On the PhD-to-industry pipeline (the stated framing):**
- "Looking back, what do you wish you'd known in your last six months of the PhD?"
- "What's changed about hiring in biopharma data/AI in 2026 versus when you made the jump?"
- "Where do you see PhDs underselling themselves in interviews — and where do they oversell?"

**Bridge to the ask:**
- "If you were me right now, where would you be looking? Companies, teams, types of roles?"
- "Is Genmab hiring on your team or adjacent — and is now a reasonable time to be having that conversation?"

---

## The Ask (rehearse out loud — 60s max)

> *"I'd love your help in two ways if you're open to it. First — if there are openings on your team or adjacent at Genmab that fit, I'd genuinely love to be considered. Second — if anyone in your network comes to mind, I'll send you a short one-pager you can forward without rewriting anything. The roles I'm targeting are biomedical AI/ML in biopharma and RWE/outcomes. I'm flexible on location and open to individual contributor or lead."*

**Why this works:** two concrete actions, gives him a clear profile to match against, and the forwardable one-pager removes all friction from the intro.

---

## Don't Do

- Lead with the resume or the ask.
- Say "AI" or "data" without a concrete technique attached.
- Ask "do you know anyone hiring?" — too open, people freeze.
- Apologize for being a PhD or frame industry as a fallback.
- Over-prepare to the point it sounds rehearsed.
